description: This file defines the interface for a ringbuffer API used in the libwebsockets project. It declares the struct lws_ring and related functions for creating, destroying, and manipulating a ring buffer, including methods for inserting, consuming, and directly accessing buffer elements. It also provides macros for managing multiple consumer tails and updating the oldest tail.

methods.name: lws_ring_create
methods.description: Creates a new ringbuffer with specified element size, count, and an optional destroy callback.

methods.name: lws_ring_destroy
methods.description: Destroys a previously created ringbuffer and frees associated resources.

methods.name: lws_ring_get_count_free_elements
methods.description: Returns the number of free elements available for insertion.

methods.name: lws_ring_get_count_waiting_elements
methods.description: Returns the number of elements waiting to be consumed from a given tail.

methods.name: lws_ring_insert
methods.description: Attempts to insert up to max_count elements from source into the ringbuffer.

methods.name: lws_ring_consume
methods.description: Attempts to consume up to max_count elements from the ringbuffer, optionally copying them into destination.

methods.name: lws_ring_get_element
methods.description: Retrieves a pointer to the next waiting element for a specified tail.

methods.name: lws_ring_update_oldest_tail
methods.description: Updates the oldest tail pointer to indicate elements are no longer in use.

methods.name: lws_ring_get_oldest_tail
methods.description: Returns the current oldest tail index.

methods.name: lws_ring_next_linear_insert_range
methods.description: Provides a linear range in the ringbuffer for direct data insertion.

methods.name: lws_ring_bump_head
methods.description: Updates the ringbuffer's head pointer after direct insertion.

methods.name: lws_ring_dump
methods.description: Outputs the current state of the ringbuffer for debugging.
